key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 60s
No history of acute febrile illness
No family history of sudden cardiac death
ECG showed sinus tachycardia and ST-segment elevation
Coronary angiography revealed normal coronary arteries
Left ventriculography confirmed systolic apical ballooning
Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT revealed a left-adrenal heterogeneous mass

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with sudden-onset chest pain, elevated troponin, and brain-type natriuretic peptide, along with the ECG findings and the confirmation of systolic apical ballooning on left ventriculography, are all consistent with Takotsubo Cardiomyopathy. The absence of coronary artery disease on angiography further supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Apical Ballooning Syndrome
rejected.why: This is another name for Takotsubo Cardiomyopathy, not a distinct diagnosis

rejected.label: Pheochromocytoma-induced Cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: Although the patient has a left-adrenal heterogeneous mass, which could be a pheochromocytoma, the primary presentation and diagnostic findings point more directly to Takotsubo Cardiomyopathy

rejected.label: Acute Coronary Syndrome
rejected.why: The coronary angiography revealed normal coronary arteries, making this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Myocardial Infarction
rejected.why: The absence of coronary artery disease and the specific pattern of apical ballooning make myocardial infarction a less fitting diagnosis
